EIA crude oil and fuel inventory report: US crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories all rose last week, pointing to a gradual normalisation of supply conditions. Gasoline stocks are rebuilding rapidly amid seasonally weaker demand, while crude and distillate inventories remain below their five-year averages, with the latter still highlighting underlying tightness in the fuel market. Meanwhile, US crude production reached a fresh record of 14.03 million barrels per day, while oil exports rebounded above 4 million barrels per day. Refinery demand also remains elevated for this time of year, supporting fuel production and inventory replenishment. Overall, the report reinforces a picture of improving supply availability and easing market tightness, although historically low distillate stocks continue to provide a degree of support to refined product prices.

#Commodities - AM note from Copenhagen:

#Copper slumped 5% yesterday to a seven-month low, pressured by global growth concerns, disappointing Chinese demand signals and expectations of increased US exports. Negative sentiment at a major industry conference in Shanghai triggered heavy speculative selling, while reports that copper could be redirected to China in December eased concerns about tight local supplies. Despite the sharp selloff, the longer-term outlook remains supported by tight scrap and mine supplies, resilient infrastructure demand and committed AI-related investment.

Precious metals: Gold extended its recent slump, touching a fresh 15-month low of USD 3,694 in Asia, as hawkish Fed minutes and Governor Waller's comments reinforced expectations of further rate hikes. Beyond higher yields and rate hike concerns, the broader commodity selloff may also reflect tightening global dollar liquidity as the dollar continues to rally. Rising AI-related financing needs, IPO activity, equity market volatility and elevated energy security costs are increasing demand for cash just as higher interest rates make funding more expensive. Gold, given its deep liquidity, and other metals may therefore be caught in a broader dash for cash, with investors selling liquid assets to meet funding needs and reduce risk exposure.

Oil: Brent trades near unchanged around USD 92 after falling 1.3% on the Wednesday. Alongside broader risk reduction across commodities, recent weakness has been driven by recovering Middle East production and exports, renewing concerns about an emerging supply glut. However, the risk of fresh disruptions remains, with the New York Times reporting that Trump, under renewed pressure from Israel's Netanyahu, is considering fresh strikes against Iran. Tehran has responded by warning neighbouring countries of retaliation should they allow US attacks to be launched from their territory.
